correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact closed-neighborhood equality condition for each vertex. Vertices sharing identical open neighborhoods are necessarily same-colored, so every multipartite part is monochromatic. If a part i has color c_i, its N[v]=V\P_i ∪ {v}, forcing T_j=q_i for j≠c_i and T_{c_i}=q_i+n_i−1, q_i=(N−n_i+1)/k. Two different-colored parts when k≥3 compare any third color to get q_i=q_h and n_i=n_h, then compare each other’s color to force both sizes 1. For k=2 comparison gives n_i+n_h=2, again singleton. Any further part is singleton by comparison with one of those of different or same color. Then G=K_r and each N[v]=V; balance iff k|r and the multinomial number of surjective equal-size partitions follows. Independent direct-definition exhaustive check over 37 profiles and 320109 assignments corroborated the classification, not used as an all-n proof.
residual_risks: Graphs must have nonempty parts, r≥2 and use exactly k≥2 colors.
The number counts labeled colors, not colorings up to color permutation.

originality.rationale: The general-k foundational source proves that identical open-neighborhood twins share a color and that k-CNBC colorability of cliques is equivalent to k dividing clique order. Its inspected text does not state this all-multipartite collapse. The two-color predecessor settles bicliques but not arbitrary r-part and k-family. Resultary matches for multipartite graphs were other coloring invariants (majority C, odd, b-coloring) with genuinely different neighborhood requirements. The structural cross-color equations provide a new complete family-level conclusion, subject to possible unindexed folklore.
residual_risks: An unindexed or folklore consequence of the known twin lemma may already be recorded elsewhere.

value.rationale: Determines the entire possible family for a recently generalized graph coloring invariant over canonical complete multipartite graphs, making the biclique negative phenomenon universal across all numbers of parts and colors and providing exact positive-case counts. It is a natural sharp structural classification, not a chosen one-off graph.
residual_risks: Only finite connected complete multipartite graphs with surjective use of k≥2 colors.
Finite enumeration is a stress test, not the infinite proof.

final_claim: A connected finite complete multipartite graph K_{n1,...,nr} (r≥2) admits a surjective closed-neighborhood-balanced k-coloring (k≥2) iff all parts have size 1 and k|r; there are r!/((r/k)!)^k labeled balanced colorings in that case.
limitations: Only finite connected complete multipartite graphs with surjective use of k≥2 colors.
Finite enumeration is a stress test, not the infinite proof.
